public_rationale: The Federal Reserve set US depository-institution reserve requirement ratios to zero effective March 26, 2020 [e1]. Its June 2026 report maintained large-bank stress capital buffer requirements at the levels disclosed in 2025 [e2]. These establish different rules for deposit reserves and capital, not the predicted consequences of failed data-center deals [e1, e2]. They do not settle the conditional forecast [e1, e2].
limitations: The packet does not establish the reserve rules for all named institution types, including private credit funds and asset managers.
No qualifying failure episode or resulting market response is documented. This does not establish that no failures occurred.
The claim gives no deadline. It leaves the jurisdiction, meaning of reserves, failure threshold and scale of unwinding unspecified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because banks, private credit funds and asset managers are not forced to keep any level of reserves, a few billion dollars of data center deals going bad is all it takes for a cataclysmic unwinding of the AI trade.
conditions: if a few billion dollars of data center deals go pear-shaped
lenders are not forced to keep any level of reserves

statement.excerpt: And because neither banks nor private credit funds nor asset managers are forced to keep any level of reserves, all it takes is a few bad apples — a few billion of data center deals — to go pear-shaped for there to be a cataclysmic unwinding of the AI trade.

from_speaker: neither banks nor private credit funds nor asset managers
forced to keep any level of reserves
a few billion of data center deals
a cataclysmic unwinding of the AI trade
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that several billion dollars of failed data-center financing would cause a severe, broad unwinding of AI investments.
Failed deal principal and lenders' realized losses must be recorded separately; the statement does not specify which amount its threshold measures.
The surrounding US financing discussion suggests US institutions, although jurisdiction is not explicit.
Cash reserve requirements must be distinguished from capital requirements. Evidence about one does not establish the absence of the other.
This is a systemic forecast, not a financial metric for a specified company.
criteria.support_condition: A documented post-publication episode involving several billion dollars of failed data-center deals, with the stated institutional premise established, causes a severe and broad unwinding of AI-linked investments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A clearly qualifying failure episode occurs under the stated conditions, its market consequences become observable, and AI investments absorb it without the predicted broad unwinding.

evidence.explanation: Supports the narrow US deposit-reserve component. It establishes neither the rules for every institution named nor the occurrence of failed data-center deals.

Banks remain subject to capital requirements. This materially qualifies any reading that zero cash reserve ratios mean no required financial safeguards, but does not resolve the conditional market forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Document a qualifying failure episode after July 22, 2026, establish the stated institutional premise, and separate failed deal principal from realized losses. Then measure whether those failures caused a severe, broad unwinding of AI investments or were absorbed without it, distinguishing their effects from unrelated shocks.
